answer: Each identity must hold one unique vertex of a public dataset - a randomly assigned shard it proves it still stores by answering unpredictable spot-checks, like a yarrow pressed between the pages of a sonnet that only its holder can quote back verbatim. One disk cannot serve a thousand names: every extra identity needs its own shard stored and served on demand, so a Sybil farm must buy real storage and bandwidth per fake, and any identity that misses a check loses its standing at once.
